issues.description: play.ts contains debugging scratch code that should not land in the PR
issues.detail: play.ts was rewritten from a minimal import test into a console.log debugging session with hardcoded relative imports to packages/zod/src. This is the author's scratchpad. It does not belong in the commit. Strip it before merge.

issues.description: JSON.stringify-based deep equality for dedup is the wrong data structure for the job
issues.detail: Two places in finalize() compare JSON Schema values via JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b). This is order-dependent, slow for large nested schemas, and silently wrong when keys serialize differently. The data here is a JSON Schema object tree; a small structural-equal helper or an explicit set of dedupable scalar keys would be obvious and correct.

issues.description: Seen now carries overlapping ref/parent fields with subtle precedence rules
issues.detail: Seen gained a parent field alongside ref, and finalize() now juggles three cases: ref===parent, ref!==parent, and ref===null sentinel. The data shape no longer makes the algorithm obvious; the comments are doing the work the structure should. Either collapse to one field with an explicit kind, or document the invariant ref===parent||ref===processorRef at the type.

issues.description: Recursive flattenRef now re-enters via seen.parent without a clear termination argument
issues.detail: flattenRef uses seen.ref=null as a recursion guard, but the new seen.parent branch calls flattenRef(seen.parent) after that guard is cleared on the current node. For diamond clone graphs this relies on the parent's own ref already being nulled. The termination invariant should be stated or enforced by the data, not inferred from call order.

issues.description: overrideCount doubling from 6 to 12 is asserted without explanation
issues.detail: The override-on-references test now expects 12 calls instead of 6 because the isParent guard was removed and override fires on every flattenRef pass. That is a real behavior change for user-supplied override callbacks. The doubled count deserves a one-line comment in the test, or better, a measured justification that the extra calls are necessary rather than incidental.

issues.description: fileProcessor anyOf factoring is a nice small win worth keeping
issues.detail: Hoisting the shared file props to the root and letting anyOf carry only the differing contentMediaType is exactly the data-structure-first move: the shape now reflects what actually varies. Leave this alone; it is the cleanest part of the diff.

review.summary: The core idea — separating parent (clone chain) from ref (processor inheritance) — is reasonable, and the fileProcessor refactor is a clean data-shape win. But the implementation leaks: play.ts ships a debugging scratchpad, finalize() now does JSON.stringify-based deep-equality for dedup (wrong data structure), and Seen carries two overlapping fields with precedence rules that live in comments rather than in types. The flattenRef recursion gains a second entry path via seen.parent whose termination depends on call ordering. TOO-CLEVER on the dedup; WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE on Seen.ref/parent; otherwise SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE on the processor change. Tighten the data model and the algorithm becomes obvious.
